semanticDecisions: each lane answers from prepared facts when they exist and never computes the facts: a one-field consumer costs a bulk window scan with early exit
strip uses Character.isWhitespace per unit and trim units at or below space; a surrogate (paired or not) is never whitespace, so the unit scans stop exactly where the stock code-point scans stop
the whitespace lanes read a 32-unit first window (most texts decide within it) and 1024-unit windows after

String.codePointCount no longer builds the code point geometry: a narrow owner answers at once, a cached geometry answers, otherwise the range is counted in bulk; random-access consumers (codePointAt, offsetByCodePoints) still build the geometry, now from bulk-read units
the empty receiver keeps its identity in trim and strip (the first build returned a new empty String; the parity test caught it)
